messages:
alex: Heads-up — customer reported SSE streaming connections that drop after ~25s and sometimes return partial output (cut mid-token). They see the client immediately reconnecting, which duplicates a few tokens on resume. Root request ID: req_9a12f. Seen across multiple regions but more in us-west-2. :eyes:

shreya: Oof. Do we have a repro? client_id or example request? Any errors in logs (gateway/proxy/runtime)?

alex: Attaching minimal repro steps they used (customer shared):
```
curl -N -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' -H 'Accept: text/event-stream' \
  'https://api.redwood-inference.com/v1/streams?model=x-large&client_id=mobile-523'
```
They reported seeing SSE heartbeats (empty comment lines) initially, then nothing, then immediate reconnects. client_id=mobile-523, trace header x-trace-id=req_9a12f included.

jamal: I pulled the packet capture the customer uploaded. Quick summary: TLS session stays up but we see the edge proxy send a FIN/RST after ~25s. The TCP-level conversation shows a FIN from proxy, then client reconnect. No TLS alert. Suspect idle timeout on the upstream LB or proxy. Extract from tcpdump:```
15:12:03.123456 IP proxy > client: Flags [F.], seq 3456, ack 7890, win 0
15:12:03.123457 IP client > proxy: Flags [R], seq 1, ack 0, win 0
```

marta: Any rate-limit / auth failures around that time? Could be our rate-limiter replacing the socket.

support-bot: Event: rate_limit.triggered - client_id=mobile-523 - rule=burst - action=close_socket - timestamp=2026-02-10T15:12:02Z

alex: Interesting — support-bot shows a rate_limit close_socket action. Customer claims they weren't spamming, just normal single stream. Also they said billing spike happened right before incident. Could billing throttle tie into route policy?

infra-bot: I pulled traces for x-trace-id=req_9a12f -> spans show upstream edge decided to cancel the stream with status code 503 when the rate-limiter hook returned "over_limit". Trace excerpt: span(edge-proxy) -> rate-limiter: decision=over_limit -> action=close_connection. Latency around decision: 10-30ms. Full trace: https://internal-traces/trace/req_9a12f

shreya: So it's not idle timeout; it's an explicit close from rate-limiter. Why did rate-limiter fire? Need config / rule evaluation logs. Jamal, can you share the exact pcap + metadata on how many concurrent streams from that customer?

jamal: Uploaded pcap to the support bucket: s3://support-pcaps/1871234567/mobile-523.pcap.gz. From pcap: client established 1 connection. But I see a previous connection from same client_id 10s prior that finished; maybe our metrics consider them bursty because of fast reconnects.

ethan: Quick note — we've had a recent rule change in burst detection to tighten thresholds for mobile clients (rolled last week). Could be a false positive. Rule: if client opens >1 connection within 15s -> close socket and record rate_limit.triggered.

marta: That matches. Customer's client does immediate reconnects on dropped SSE (no backoff), so they can trigger the burst rule on reconnection loops. We should change behavior for streaming endpoints: instead of close_socket, mark over_limit and respond with 429 headers or an SSE comment advising backoff. Closing the socket causes partial outputs and duplication.

shreya: Agreed. Short-term mitigation: rollback the burst rule change for streaming routes or exclude routes with Accept: text/event-stream. Jamal / infra — can we add an exception today?

jamal: I can push a config patch to exclude content-type SSE for the burst rule. Patching now to route-match header 'Accept: text/event-stream' -> bypass close_socket. Will monitor.

support-bot: Action queued: policy.patch - id=patch_394 - target=rate-limiter - condition=header('Accept') contains 'text/event-stream' - action=allow_socket - requested_by=jamal

infra-bot: Also recommend adding a keepalive ping on client side. For SSE we can emit a `:ping\n\n` comment every 20s to prevent intermediate proxies from idling, but in this case the logic was explicit close, so the patch is primary.

alex: For the customer: ask them to update client to exponential backoff on reconnect (start 1s -> 2s -> 4s) and include resume token in query param so duplicated tokens are deduped server-side. Also ask them to send a new pcap after the patch is live.

marta: I'll draft response and create a customer ticket with remediation steps, link to the patch, and request for new pcap if they still see it.

ethan: Follow-up tasks: 1) Rollback/patch burst rule for SSE routes (jamal) 2) Add monitoring alert for rate_limit.close_socket spikes on streaming endpoints (marta) 3) Add instrumentation to rate-limiter decision logs to include route and header matches (infra) 4) Postmortem if customer impact > X (shreya).

alex: One more debugging tip to ask customer if they can run a short tcpdump focused on their client: `sudo tcpdump -w /tmp/stream.pcap host api.redwood-inference.com and port 443` and upload. Also ask for SDK version.

jamal: Patch applied to canary. Observability: rate_limit.close_socket events for streaming routes dropped to 0 on canary after patch. Monitor for 30m before global rollout.

marta: Customer reply draft: "Thanks — we found your resume token and client logs helpful. We've patched our rate-limit configuration to avoid prematurely closing SSE sockets. Please upgrade client to the latest SDK which implements reconnect backoff and resume. If you still see partial output, please re-run tcpdump and attach bundle. We'll keep monitoring." :+1:

shreya: Nice runbook additions: add a checklist for support to check rate_limit.triggered, tracing header, pcap, and whether route is SSE. Put into KB under support/streaming-triage.

alex: sounds good. I'll mark this resolved for now but will keep thread open until 24h monitoring window completes. :eyes:
